subject: Pilot: billing quantum, context-floor, and pilot discount clarification
messages:
From: John Miller <jmiller@acme-retail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot billing questions: short chats, rollovers, and discount

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. A couple of billing questions came up while our procurement and engineering teams reviewed the pilot scope (attached is our internal pilot SOW). Can you confirm the following before we sign?

1) How are very short interactions billed? Example: a user sends a 6-token prompt and receives an 8-token reply — is there a minimum charge per API call, and do you round up?
2) For the committed pilot, do unused committed tokens roll over month-to-month? If not, can we convert unused commitment into account credit?
3) Pricing for burst vs sustained: if we provision Dedicated capacity vs Hosted plan, does the rounding/quantum change?

We want to make sure we can model our expected spend (we expect a lot of low-token interactions). Also, procurement asked about a starter discount for the first three months while we ramp — what flexibility do you have?

Thanks,
John Miller
Head of Engineering
Acme Retail

Attachment: pilot-sow-acme-v1.pdf (PDF, 187KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <jmiller@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Sara Diaz <sara.diaz@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot billing questions: short chats, rollovers, and discount

John — thanks for sending the SOW and the clear questions. Short answers up front and details below:

- Billing unit: we charge on (input_tokens + output_tokens). For Hosted (standard) inference we bill in a 16-token quantum and apply a per-request minimum of 64 tokens — so your 6+8 example would be billed as 64 tokens. For Dedicated (reserved) capacity, billing is measured against committed token-units where 1 token-unit = 256 tokens; Dedicated usage rounds to the nearest token-unit for monthly metering.

- Rolling/unused commitments: by default committed token-units for Dedicated do not roll over as one-to-one unused tokens. As a concession for pilots, we can convert unused units into account credit valid up to 90 days after the month of commitment (credit equals 50% of list value of unused units).

- Burst vs sustained: the quantum and minimums differ as noted above (Hosted: 16-token quantum + 64-token min; Dedicated: 256-token unit metering). Streaming responses are accumulated per session and aggregated into quanta within a 30-second window where possible; if aggregation isn't possible the per-request minimum still applies.

Pilot discount proposal (flexible):
- Option A (faster ramp): 15% off list for first 3 months + one-time pilot credit of 250,000 tokens applied to Hosted charges.
- Option B (committed): 25% off list on committed token-units for first 6 months if you commit >= 3,000 token-units/month (3,000 * 256 tokens).

Before I finalize, I need a quick sign-off from our finance and legal teams on the rollover-as-credit language and the exact discount structure. Copying Neha (finance) and Marcus (legal) to confirm we can offer the pilot credit and the 90-day credit conversion flow.

Next step: tell me which discount option you prefer and we’ll attach the concession to the SOW.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)

John / Sara — updating you after internal review. Short version of confirmed terms for the pilot:

1) Billing quantum and minimums
- Hosted (pilot): charges = input + output tokens; billed to the nearest 16-token quantum with a per-request floor of 64 tokens. Aggregation: when requests originate from the same session within a 30-second window we attempt to aggregate for billing quanta; where aggregation is not possible the 64-token floor still applies.
- Dedicated (if you choose reserved capacity): metered against 256-token "token-units" at month end; rounding occurs to the nearest whole token-unit.

2) Unused committed units / rollovers
- For this pilot only we will convert unused Dedicated token-units into account credit at 50% of list price. Credit is valid for 90 days after the month in which the commitment was made. We cannot issue cash refunds — only account credit.

3) Pilot discount & credits (agreed)
- Agreed pilot package: Option A accepted — 15% off list for first 3 months on Hosted usage + one-time 250,000 token credit applied to your account.

4) Next steps and paperwork
- I will attach the concession to the SOW and route to DocuSign. Marcus confirmed the rollover-as-credit language and asked to add: "Credits are non-transferable and expire after 90 days; Redwood retains the right to audit usage to prevent misuse."
- Neha confirmed finance is OK with the 250k credit for this pilot.

If that matches your expectation, reply with "ACK" and we’ll send the updated SOW for signature. If you prefer Option B (committed 3,000 token-units/month for 6 months at 25% off), let me know and I’ll get updated pricing and SOW language.

Thanks — excited to get this pilot started.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
